target_customer: Buyers and sellers of AI compute capacity (labs, cloud and GPU owners, financial firms)
problem: AI compute is bought through opaque bilateral deals; Liquid Compute (formerly Pluto) builds a marketplace and a CFTC-regulated exchange for cash-settled and physically settled compute contracts.
business_model: Exchange and marketplace (trading and clearing fees, market data; assumed)
product_category: Fintech infrastructure: compute exchange and derivatives

technical_complexity.rationale: Requires exchange and clearing infrastructure plus regulatory approval (DCM and DCO applications pending with CFTC) and standardizing compute contracts.

defensibility.rationale: If CFTC licenses are granted they would be hard to replicate; not yet granted.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Per 2026 reports ICE partnered with Ornn on GPU futures (May 2026) and CME plans compute futures (Oct 2026); these came well after the batch.

market_need_then: Compute scarcity and price volatility; the CFTC later sought comment on whether compute is standardized enough for futures. No dated 2024-2025 evidence fetched.

brand_strength.rationale: Rebranded from Pluto, name meaning not sourced; no brand press found.

outcome_analysis: Liquid Compute, formerly Pluto, went through YC and in September 2026 announced a $15M seed co-led by FirstMark and Chemistry while its CFTC applications remain pending. It rides AI compute scarcity but depends on regulatory approval and faces ICE and CME entering compute futures. Too early to judge success.
notes: Batch conflict: directory says Winter 2025; sources say W24 or W25; founded year 2024 or 2025, left null. Seed cross-checked: Pulse2 fetched; HPCwire, Dealroom and others report it in search listings (not fetched). Competitors (Ornn, CME, ICE) are dated 2026, so not recorded as at founding. Whether the new compute-futures sector had dated competitors in early 2025 is unknown. Name origin not found.
